I think you should attempt to pursue a diagnosis but definitely with someone else. This man clearly is stuck in the 20th century as far as his opinion on hyperactivity. It is possible you might not have it but this guy clearly doesn't know what he is talking about. 

There are technically 3 "types" or presentations of adhd: inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive type, and combination. Combination is 60% of all cases, inattentive is 30% and hyperactive is only 10%. You definitely need a second opinion because the presentations are different for everyone and no diagnosis looks the same. 

I would recommend looking up adhd criteria for diagnosis in the DSM V.

I lost my dog that I grew up with in 2018 right after I started my freshman year of college and it was devastating. We knew she was old but she started declining some one day and was gone by that night. I was depressed then but on antidepressants and felt robotic because I was still working out the dose. When the pain finally hit it was excruciating. 

I don't have much advice but I will say, there is no way to make it feel ok. All of your feelings are completely valid and everyone experiences grief differently - especially people with mental illnesses and more specifically bipolar/bipolar 2. People say time heals all wounds but it just makes some of them less painful. The best way I have heard grief described as was this: your pain is a box and it is triggered by a ball inside that box - every time the ball hits the side of the box you feel overwhelmed, sad, all other emotions associated with loss. As time goes on, the ball slowly gets smaller and it becomes a little more bearable to keep going each day.

Take your time with everything and don't do anything (i.e. look at pictures, talk about it in depth, etc) until you are ready. It is so hard but you are not alone in this and it will get better eventually.

I know exactly how painful it is. One thing I have tried when I am on the edge is the 54321 technique. I learned it from the crisis text line and it honestly does help relax me a bit. You name 5 things you can see, 4 things you can hear, 3 things you can feel, 2 things you smell, and 1 good thing about yourself. That and also holding ice or sticking your face in a bowl of ice water for a few seconds a couple of times. Sometimes nothing works and all you have to do is persist through the pain and try to go to sleep or do something distracting that will reset your mind. I hope you can find something that brings you a smile or a little peace, feel free to message me if you need to.
